judgements.justification: A's Reviewer_ecPK cut 6 to 5 in an edit dated 2021-09-06, a month after the author response, on a new mechanism-specificity objection the authors never answered, and A's meta-review repeated it as open; B's main objection (eGa2) came early and was refuted.
The scores are not near-identical (A 5, 7, 6, 5 against B 8, 7, 6, 6) and the arguments differ, so the split does not come from tier thresholds applied to the same reviews.
A's most careful reviewer, ecPK, had their doubt repeated in A's meta-review, and B's confidence-5 reviewer eGa2 withdrew their objection, so no area chair passed over an expert verdict.

A's concerns (tightness, mechanism specificity, writing, matrix mechanism) were as answerable by clarification as B's, and epzC in A did rise on the response; the gap comes from a late unanswered objection, not from concerns no response could fix.
A has no single outlier (two 5s), and B's remaining scores without bo89's 8 (7, 6, 6) do not match A's 5, 7, 6, 5, so no one score alone set the tier.
The only outlier, B's champion bo89, gave an 8 the response had no reason to revise; A's silent WJWj is not an outlier in a 5/5/6/7 panel.
A's area chair did not set aside a low score as unreliable; it called the reviews divided, repeated the detractors' doubt and accepted on significance.
Neither committee raised audience breadth or venue fit; both stressed the paper's importance for official statistics.

A's meta-review repeated ecPK's open doubt, which the authors had in fact not answered, and B's meta-review restated the result correctly, so neither misreported the reviewers' positions or the rebuttal.
In each committee two of four reviewers engaged with the response (A: epzC, ecPK; B: eGa2, NcCk), so neither committee's majority left it unanswered.
No reviewer who said they could not verify the results gave a clear accept: ecPK, who was unfamiliar with the technique, gave 5, and B's low-confidence NcCk gave a marginal 6.

A's area chair named the split, repeated the detractors' doubt and accepted on its own view of significance rather than adopting one side's critique, and the split moved the tier only through the scores.
The notes record no conflicting results or accounts across the two responses; the reliance on [3] and the interpretive novelty appear in both committees.
B's eGa2 cited Blum, Ligett and Roth wrongly but conceded and raised to 6, and A's WJWj's incrementality claim relative to [3] was checked as correct, so no wrong novelty verdict fed a final score.
B's area chair chose a spotlight on 8, 7, 6, 6, two of them 'marginally above' and the 8 thinly argued, and the meta-review gives no reason for that tier.
No reviewer objected to the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises; the objections were technical (proof steps, mechanism specificity, prior work).
Neither committee had an engaged champion: B's 8 from bo89 is mostly summary with only '[response acknowledged]' after the rebuttal, and A's 7 from dx3d is generic praise.
Both committees accepted, and neither rejected the paper because the promised revisions needed another round of review.
Both meta-reviews rest on the visible reviews and the area chairs' own reading; no off-record assessment appears.
WJWj's request for practical implications was an omission the authors conceded and promised to fix, not a standard for the contribution type that A applied and B did not.
A's two 5s rest on central points (whether the trade-off holds for all mechanisms, the proof's group-privacy step, tightness, incrementality), not on peripheral ones.
